parsed.explanation: The operative regime combines the governing state's protective anti-discrimination law (gender identity, penal and labour code) with a documented, unremedied birth-sex prison-placement practice affecting any detainee on the island, and a watchdog record of persistent fundamental-rights violations (~40 referrals since 2010) with no shown remedy. Detention exposure is real but low-frequency in a low-crime, discretionary, luxury-tourism society with no documented hostility toward trans or gay visitors. Care access is a practical exposure for visitors dependent on local treatment. Net: above the Elevated band's floor, but held below Reduced-risk anchors with working remedies by the custody placement and unremedied institutional record.

entry_documents.exposure: None documented; the state's identity and document framework applies and no border friction for trans visitors is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: National legal gender-marker change without surgery; anti-discrimination law covers gender identity.
entry_documents.interaction: Document regime is national; island applies it unchanged.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detainees fall under the state's prison administration recognising only biological sex; trans women held under birth sex (2011 men's-prison placement); watchdog found serious rights violations persisting with no shown remediation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any island detention routes into the national birth-sex placement system; low-crime environment makes detention itself infrequent.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Hospital or facility placement by birth sex is not specifically documented, but the national custody policy is the documented facility exposure.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National administration controls island detention facilities.

care_services.exposure: Prescriptions and ongoing gender-affirming care cannot be assumed locally; specialist provision not assured on an 8-square-mile island of ~10,000.
care_services.protection: Hormone therapy and surgery lawful under the national framework since 1975; visitors can carry supplies.
care_services.interaction: Care gap is a climate/capacity constraint reaching visitors directly if treatment runs out.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Not documented; no police hostility, raids, or profiling of trans people recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Gender identity protected in penal and labour codes since 2012/2016; police climate appears neutral.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Low-crime discretion-oriented society reduces police contact probability.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not specifically documented; same care-capacity and custody-placement exposures would apply to a travelling minor if detained or needing care.
minors_guardians.protection: National anti-discrimination coverage applies regardless of age.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented; sources record no hostility toward gay or trans visitors; low crime.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hospitality trained for diverse clientele; legal recourse under anti-discrimination law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Discretion, not permissiveness: no venues or scene, but absence of hostility is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Watchdog recommendations appear unimplemented; no documented remedy reversing birth-sex custody placement; no island-specific travel advice exists.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National anti-discrimination and penal-code recourse exists in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse for custody placement is not shown to work; local deputy's vote against the 2013 marriage law is a climate signal only.

anchor_checks.comparison: Marisol Union's ward-by-document assignment with weak remedies resembles this dossier's birth-sex custody placement with recurring watchdog findings and no shown remediation. This jurisdiction's exposure reaches only detainees (rarer in a low-crime setting) and its social climate is more openly welcoming, so it sits somewhat above 0.55-C.

Vellmaris shows a hostile checkpoint incident but functioning courts, compensation, and reliable release. Here no hostile incident is documented and the law protects, but the custody placement is unremedied and recurring — the remedy gap is worse than 0.65-A's working complaint system, pulling this slightly below 0.65.

Meridia at 0.75 offers trained border officers, working tribunal remedies and compensation for unlawful detention. This jurisdiction lacks any documented working remedy for its worst feature (birth-sex placement), and care access is materially constrained, so it cannot reach 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime pairs strong national anti-discrimination law and a documented, discreetly welcoming tourism society with no recorded trans-specific hostility — strong everyday-climate evidence — against one serious documented exposure: any detainee enters a national prison system that places trans women under birth sex, with a watchdog recording persistent violations and recommendations not shown to have been implemented. Under the band implications, unremedied universal custody exposure with no working remedy keeps the jurisdiction out of a solid Reduced-risk score, while low detention likelihood, absence of street hostility, and protective law keep it well above High Risk. The care-capacity gap is a real, manageable exposure. Net rating: 0.63.
